title: BKLO simultaneous perfect matchings and spread matchings
abstract: Formalizes the r = 2 specialization of the simultaneous factor-selection step in BKLO Lemma 10.7: under quantitative parity, minimum-degree, codegree, and incidence hypotheses, a linearly sized, overlapping family of neighbourhood graphs admits perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof replaces the published randomized greedy process by a deterministic pessimistic-estimator sweep. Supporting results develop perfect, near-perfect, edge-disjoint, and quantitatively weighted spread matchings from sharp minimum-degree hypotheses.

informal.BKLOK2.lemma107K2_holds: Specializes BKLO Lemma 10.7 to r = 2 in its apex-neighbourhood configuration: for every sufficiently large admissible configuration, all indexed neighbourhood graphs admit perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof is deterministic.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_isPerfectMatching_of_: Every finite simple graph of even order whose minimum degree is at least half its order has a perfect matching.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_isMatching_compl_sing: Every finite simple graph of odd order n and minimum degree at least (n - 1) / 2 has a matching whose vertex set is the complement of a singleton.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_involutions_pairwise_: If every vertex of a finite even vertex set has at least half the set size plus t neighbors inside the set, then the graph contains t + 1 pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings of that set, represented by an indexed family of partner involutions. These involutions are pairwise distinct when the vertex set is nonempty.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_spread_involution: Under the same minimum-degree condition with slack t, every nonnegative edge-weight function admits a perfect matching whose weight is at most 1 / (t + 1) times the total weight over ordered pairs in the vertex set.
